records.title: Quito Metro Line 1
aliases: Primera Línea del Metro de Quito
records.answer: Quito's first metro line connects fifteen stations between Quitumbe and Labrador. Its operating account combines substantial trip volumes with maintenance restrictions and published service patterns; a proposed northern extension remains separate from the railway already carrying passengers.
records.scope: One original Quitumbe–Labrador metro line. Its stations and operating subsystems are components, not additional projects; the proposed La Ofelia extension is future context and is not counted as operating infrastructure or a separate addition here.
records.stage: Commercial operation began December 1, 2023. September 2026 totals and the October service-page update describe an operating line; survey scores, reference frequencies and financing support for an extension do not establish uninterrupted service or extension delivery.

identity_decision.rationale: Count the original Quito Metro Line 1 once between Quitumbe and Labrador. Do not count its fifteen stations, maintenance contracts or proposed La Ofelia extension as additional projects. Quito's metropolitan municipality is a separate place identity, and no national acquisition docket is reused to manufacture a second project count.

timeline.event: Commercial operation began, as reported in the municipality's December 5 account.
Owner explained rail-defect precautions and planned corrective work; the page displays two February header dates.
A 434-user survey and service interruptions occurred during the month described in the May release.
Municipality described CAF support for four proposed stations toward La Ofelia.
Municipality published January–April trips, survey results and the maintenance account.
Cutoff for the homepage's cumulative trip total.
Service page records its information review, retaining August reference frequencies.

sections.heading: One operating line and a defined opening
sections.text: Quito's first metro line links Quitumbe in the south with Labrador in the north through fifteen stations. The current service page describes a 22-kilometre route, while the municipality's December 2023 report dates commercial operation to December 1. Those facts identify the existing railway without adding proposed northern stations to its operating footprint. Stations, train operations and the municipal territory are related but different objects. A resident's journey may continue beyond either terminus, so the line's own route and published travel time should not be mistaken for the total time needed to reach a home, job or service.

sections.heading: Trips and survey ratings answer different questions
sections.text: The operator's homepage reports 173,281,818 cumulative trips through September 30, 2026, including 5,604,799 during September. These are journeys, not distinct people. A separate May municipal release reports 21.6 million trips during January–April and describes an April survey of 434 users. Respondents rated the service highly, including accessibility and perceived safety. That survey describes participating users' assessments, not measured lift availability or an independent safety audit. The periods and populations must remain explicit: cumulative use, a monthly flow and a sample's opinion cannot be combined into one performance score or substituted for one another.

sections.heading: Maintenance creates operating constraints
sections.text: The owner's February 2025 maintenance explanation records rail fissures identified in late October 2024 and a speed reduction at the affected point. It also describes corrective procurement difficulties and planned repair and testing. That historical plan is not a repair-completion receipt, nor evidence that the defect remains unresolved today. The May 2026 release separately acknowledges an April communications-related suspension and temporary frequency adjustments during wheel reprofiling. These examples show why maintenance and use belong in the same account. A large passenger total can coexist with interruptions; it does not measure their duration, passenger impact or recovery quality.

sections.heading: Northern expansion remains a future stage
sections.text: The May 11 municipal account describes CAF backing of USD 80 million for an extension toward La Ofelia with four additional stations. It presents expected connectivity and journey-time benefits for the northern catchment. Reported credit approval is not disbursement, accepted construction or passenger operation. The original line remains the counted operating project, while the extension needs its own procurement, construction and commissioning sequence before its benefits can be reported as delivered. The source's inconsistent description of elapsed operating years is not used to change the established December 2023 opening date or create a new chronology.

sections.heading: A timetable is a reference for a journey
sections.text: The service page reviewed October 7 lists weekday operation from 05:30 to 23:00 and reference intervals of five minutes at peak times and eight off-peak, attributed to an August 2026 bulletin. It also advertises a 34-minute terminal-to-terminal journey. These are published service references, not observed November headways or a guarantee for a particular trip. The distinction matters when a rider needs to coordinate onward transport, work or care responsibilities. Special notices and current conditions can alter the journey; a retrospective service assessment instead needs actual departures, cancellations and access conditions for a defined period.

sections.heading: Evidence test for the next operating account
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: follow a fixed operating period with actual train intervals, cancellations, passenger loads and station-access outages, preserving the denominator behind each measure. Join maintenance interventions to their acceptance and return-to-service records rather than treating work announcements as closure. Keep survey design and respondent composition beside satisfaction results, and distinguish repeated trips from the number of people reached. For La Ofelia, follow financing, construction and passenger opening separately. These records would explain whether increased use is accompanied by a more dependable whole journey without crediting a planned extension for benefits it has not yet delivered.

next_artifacts: Period-specific observed headways, cancellations and passenger-delay records.
Rail and wheel intervention acceptance and return-to-service records.
Survey method and accessible-route equipment availability for the same period.
La Ofelia financing execution, construction and commissioning artifacts.

records.title: Lima–Callao Metro Line 2 and Line 4 branch
aliases: Línea 2 del Metro de Lima y Callao
records.answer: Lima–Callao's concession combines an operating five-station section with much larger railway works. Excavation, systems installation, card access and station accessibility have different tests; none makes the full planned corridor operational by implication.
records.scope: One integrated Line 2 and contracted Line 4 branch project: 27 km plus an 8 km branch. The five-station Etapa 1A is the operating subset; later stages, individual stations and the wider future Line 4 are not additional counted projects here.
records.stage: Etapa 1A opened December 21, 2023. A July 2026 report records completion of Line 2 tunnel excavation, while the August regulator account still describes installation and future operating forecasts. Card requirements and a November personalization-restoration notice concern access, not full-corridor opening.

identity_decision.rationale: Count the named Line 2 concession with its contracted Line 4 branch once, preserving the distinction between the five operating stations and remaining works. The branch is not the entire future Line 4, and each stage, tunnel section, station or city district is not a new project. No existing national acquisition docket is reused.

timeline.event: The concessionaire dates the start of Etapa 1A operation to this day.
Card-access notice bears this publication date; its current wording refers retrospectively to July 8.
Concessionaire reported completion of the 27 km Line 2 tunnel excavation.
Transport-card validation requirement took effect under the published notice.
Ositrán reported separate construction progress and future operation forecasts for later stages.
Congress news centre described a visit to operating, testing and maintenance facilities.
Concessionaire announced restoration of card-personalization service at ticket offices.

sections.heading: The concession is larger than the operating section
sections.text: The project combines a 27-kilometre east–west Line 2 with an eight-kilometre branch of the future Line 4. Together these form the named contract scope, not two fully operating lines. The concessionaire dates Etapa 1A's opening to December 21, 2023, with five stations between Evitamiento and Mercado Santa Anita. Its published investment commitment of USD 4,531 million excludes IGV and is not final audited expenditure. The remaining stages must pass their own delivery tests. Planned route length, automation capability and future passenger demand should therefore remain distinct from the small portion already providing service.

sections.heading: Excavation completion is not railway opening
sections.text: The July 2 construction report says the Delia machine's arrival at Insurgentes completed excavation of the 27-kilometre Line 2 tunnel. This is a substantial civil-works milestone, not acceptance of the complete railway. Ositrán's August account reports separate construction progress for stage 1B, stage 2 and the branch, while describing remaining power, non-railway and automated-operation systems. Its 2029 and 2030 operation dates are forecasts in that dated release. Neither high construction percentages nor a continuous excavated tunnel prove that stations, trains, control systems and emergency arrangements are ready together for passenger service.

sections.heading: A free journey can still require a card
sections.text: The published access notice makes transport-card validation mandatory from July 8, 2026, while stating that the journey does not require a fare payment or card recharge. The general card purchase costs S/7.50; that is not the price of each trip. This distinction matters for someone arriving at a station expecting entirely frictionless free access. A separate November 18 notice reports restored card-personalization service at ticket offices. It concerns one administrative function, not uninterrupted train operation. Documentation, card issuance and the actual journey should be followed separately rather than folded into a single statement that the system is available.

sections.heading: Physical access is a route through the station
sections.text: The operator's accessibility page describes lifts, escalators, tactile paving, wheelchair access, priority spaces, alarms and assistance. It also directs riders to ask the service line about the condition of their accessible route. That distinction is important: installed equipment is not the same as its live availability. A usable journey requires the relevant entrance, vertical circulation, platform and train space to work together. The description does not provide a measured uptime series or prove the condition of a particular station today. No call or station inspection was performed, so current individual routing remains outside this account.

sections.heading: Oversight and delivery responsibilities remain distinct
sections.text: The Congress news centre's August 26 account describes a visit to the first stage's operating, testing and maintenance facilities and records discussion of project delays. The concessionaire emphasizes coordination between public and private participants. Parliamentary commentary about administrative obstacles is not an independent causal evaluation of those delays, and a site visit is not an acceptance certificate. Ositrán's separate construction report provides another institutional perspective, but its future dates remain forecasts. Keeping these roles visible helps readers distinguish political attention, contractual supervision and technical readiness instead of treating every official appearance as a new delivery decision.

sections.heading: Evidence test from tunnel to connected service
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: follow each remaining stage from civil completion through installed systems, integrated tests, formal acceptance and passenger opening. Preserve the operating subset so its passenger counts are not presented as use of the whole contract. For service access, track card-issuance interruptions and station-route equipment outages separately from train cancellations. Retain the tax and scope basis of investment figures, and compare actual milestones with the forecasts that preceded them. These records would show where delivery is advancing and where residents still face constraints without converting construction progress into an unsupported claim of full network readiness.

next_artifacts: Stage-specific system integration, acceptance and passenger-opening records.
Actual operating limits and observed service performance for Etapa 1A.
Accessible-route outage/restoration and card-service interruption records.
Comparable contract-cost and schedule revisions with tax and scope definitions.

records.title: Quito metropolitan services
records.answer: Quito's metropolitan services extend beyond the metro corridor into urban and rural parishes. Water maintenance, investment plans, educational transitions, individual property titles and shared local facilities reveal different parts of how the district serves its residents.
records.scope: One Distrito Metropolitano de Quito, including its urban and rural parish context, not the whole province of Pichincha or a wider water catchment. Illustrative canals, treatment proposals, childcare centres and neighbourhood works do not create additional counted identities.
records.stage: Dated municipal accounts report a bounded canal repair, childcare-place allocations, property regularization and local works, alongside water investments at mixed planning and procurement stages. These are not universal service delivery, independently audited results or one combined city-performance score.

identity_decision.rationale: Count Quito once as the metropolitan district rather than only its metro corridor or the wider Pichincha province. Urban and rural parish examples remain inside that one place account. Do not turn the water portfolio, individual titles, childcare centres or forty-three reported local works into extra project/place identities or reuse a historical country docket.

timeline.event: Municipality presented a mixed-stage water, sanitation and drainage investment portfolio.
Municipality published its account of forty-three works in Calderón and Llano Chico; the exact ceremony date is not assigned.
EPMAPS completed the described 42-metre Pita canal repair, according to the May 4 report.
Municipality reported allocation of 524 educational-continuity places.
Municipal regularization account reported an aggregate title count over a little more than three years.

sections.heading: Water continuity depends on maintained components
sections.text: EPMAPS reported completing a 42-metre repair to the Pita canal on May 2, 2026. The canal carries raw water to the Puengasí treatment plant, so this is one upstream component of a longer supply chain. The May 4 account describes controlled emptying, surface preparation, pipe installation and progressive refilling, and identifies the work as the third repaired section in that area. This is a bounded maintenance completion, not a measurement of uninterrupted household supply throughout Quito. To understand the resident's experience, plant operation, distribution conditions and household service must remain connected but separately measured parts of the account.

sections.heading: The water portfolio contains different stages
sections.text: The municipality's January investment presentation groups nine projects in drinking water, sanitation and storm drainage, with an indicative portfolio of around USD 100 million. Some items concern studies or consultancy, others procurement or works. The proposed Quito wastewater plant, expansion at El Troje and Solanda drainage therefore cannot all be described as completed infrastructure. Nor does an investor presentation prove that every item has secured financing. The portfolio helps explain where the utility intends to expand capacity and address urban growth, but actual treatment, flood reduction and household continuity need their own commissioning and operating records.

sections.heading: Early care and education require a handover
sections.text: The July 15 municipal account reports 524 places assigned for children leaving Quito Wawas to enter municipal early-education centres. It describes coordination between the municipal social-service unit and education secretariat, with allocation considering proximity and vulnerability. Those criteria connect care to a family's everyday geography rather than treating a place anywhere in the district as equally usable. Assigned places are not confirmed attendance or a longitudinal educational outcome. The official indexed report was available after direct retrieval timed out; its wider centre totals are not used to claim universal access or a complete district-wide service denominator.

sections.heading: A property title is not a newly delivered home
sections.text: Quito's November regularization account explains the difference between an undivided interest in a larger land parcel and an individual title identifying a household's plot. It reports 9,574 titles delivered across 313 consolidated settlements over a little more than three years. This is a municipal program claim, not an independently audited register or a count of newly built homes. The distinction matters because title, safe construction and utility connections are different conditions. Regularization can address tenure uncertainty without proving that every associated service has been supplied. No individual property record was queried or legal determination made here.

sections.heading: Rural parishes need streets and shared facilities
sections.text: The February account of Calderón and Llano Chico describes forty-three local works spanning roads, parks, community buildings and public-service spaces. Landázuri illustrates how a community house, children's play space and paved streets can serve related daily needs. These are municipal handover claims, not an independent assessment of long-term condition or use. The works are examples within one metropolitan place, not forty-three additional portfolio projects. The source's cost table has inconsistent formatting, so it is not summed into an audited expenditure total. Maintenance and access after the ceremony remain essential to whether the facilities continue serving residents.

sections.heading: Evidence test for a district-wide service account
sections.text: Editorial evidence test: keep urban and rural parish conditions visible without assigning one system's results to the whole district. Follow water repairs through plant and household continuity, investment proposals through acceptance and operation, and educational allocations through actual attendance and subsequent transitions. Pair property titles with separately evidenced services and housing conditions. For shared facilities, retain the handover, maintenance responsibility and later use. The metro is one important connection within this wider account, not a substitute for neighbourhood services. These separate records would make uneven delivery visible while avoiding an unsupported synthetic score for Quito.

next_artifacts: Plant and distribution continuity/quality records linked to the repaired canal component.
Project-specific financing, commissioning and operating records for the water portfolio.
Actual attendance and transition outcomes for the allocated education cohort.
Aggregate title-register reconciliation and separately measured utility/housing conditions.
Dated maintenance and use records for the handed-over parish facilities.
